What the numbers say

For the session of Wednesday, November 18, 2026, the DappGo regime model reads the tracked universe (101 Taiwan-listed names: the 100 largest companies by market value plus the 0050 ETF) as risk-off. The TAIEX is below its 50-day average and below its 200-day average; its 20-day trend is down and realised volatility is in the high band.

5 of 101 tickers (5%) are priced above their own 20-day moving average, and 46 of 101 (46%) above their 200-day average. Below 30% is the level the model treats as weak breadth, which is enough on its own for a risk-off reading. On the day 54 rose and 44 fell, with 3 unchanged; the median move was +0.37%.

Among sectors with at least two tracked names, Networking and AI hardware had the strongest average move at +3.43% and Plastics and petrochemicals the weakest at −3.78%, a spread of 7.21 percentage points. The standard deviation of sector averages was 2.21 points; a larger figure means sectors moved less in step.

17 tickers have a 14-day RSI at or below 30 (3702, 2347, 2356, 2382, 2059, 2337 and 11 more), and 1 at or above 70 (2412). An RSI extreme records how one-sided recent trading has been. It is not, by itself, evidence that the move is about to reverse.

Summed over the 101 names with institutional data, foreign investors' five-day position is net selling of 148,271 lots and investment trusts' is net selling of 250,745 lots (one lot is 1,000 shares). The two groups are on the same side.

Against the previous session in this archive (2026-11-17), the share of tickers above the 20-day average moved from 10% to 5%, and the regime reading stayed risk-off.
